requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Where illustrations appear, they show independently composed natural subjects with visible ink marks and transparent colour washes. Simplified incidental texture and different poses or crops are acceptable; photographs substituted for commissioned illustrations, opaque rendering throughout, or invented diagnostic anatomy fail. An index or form need not contain an illustration.

Assess each depicted supplied species against its relevant features. Adult robin: orange-red face and breast, brown back, pale belly. Adult blue tit: blue cap and wings, white face with dark eye stripe, greenish back, yellow underparts and fine short beak; its overview shows it resting on a twig. Daisy: white rays and yellow centre on a slender stalk connected to a rooted low rosette of spoon-shaped leaves. Clover: an intact leaf normally has three leaflets joined at one point, beside a rounded white or pinkish head; pale markings may vary. Adult ladybird: red wing cases with three black spots on each side and one shared near the front, plus black-and-white thorax markings. Snail: mottled coiled shell attached to its body and two long upper tentacles; lower tentacles can be small or hidden. Detail crops may isolate the named feature, and natural occlusion is allowed; the ladybird overview must still communicate the seven-spot arrangement. Unrelated plants in reference backgrounds must not become daisy anatomy.

Reader-facing language and activities suit children aged 8–12 with adults, and depicted outings fit brief daytime observation in English town parks or gardens. Broader seasonal species facts and nighttime snail behaviour may be explained without changing the activity setting. Foreign reference-photo locations must not be presented as the book's outing locations, and the six subjects must remain possible encounters rather than guaranteed sightings.

The cover visibly carries the required title, subtitle and age label and an original illustration of one or more supplied species. Its typography, layout palette and illustration treatment implement the preceding specification; the depicted species retains its supplied diagnostic appearance.

Require these exact name and folio assignments: European robin / Erithacus rubecula, 4–5; Blue tit / Cyanistes caeruleus, 6–7; Common daisy / Bellis perennis, 8–9; White clover / Trifolium repens, 10–11; 7-spot ladybird / Coccinella septempunctata, 12–13; Garden snail / Cornu aspersum, 14–15. Each spread has three concise supplied-meaning facts, two or more correctly attached feature labels, and one question faithful to its supplied observation prompt. Technical terms are explained beside first use. Fact selection and paraphrasing may vary; wrong biology, names, folios or label connections fail.

Each artwork reads as two facing portrait pages in the nominal 148:210 page proportion, with two text columns per page and a visible grid consistent with 66 mm columns, a 4 mm gap, 6 mm outer margins and a 6 mm protected band on each side of the central fold. Text, labels and diagnostic features stay outside protected bands; background washes may enter them. Judge relative geometry rather than exact raster dimensions. Both assigned folios appear on their corresponding pages: method 2–3, overviews 4–15 in species order, details 16–27 in the same order, bird comparison 28–29, flower comparison 30–31, places 32–33, questions 34–35, index 36–37, blank record 38–39 and worked record 40–41.

Typography, rules, panels and other layout elements use the specified dark green, pale green and rust system, with all three present on the tier-6 overview, index and blank-record spreads. Allow substrate white, transparency, antialiasing and small reproduction shifts. Natural organism colours are independent of the three layout inks. Substituting a different layout palette or recolouring diagnostic organism patches to match it fails.

Read the index as a complete navigation record headed Find a neighbour. It must pair European robin / Erithacus rubecula with 4–5; Blue tit / Cyanistes caeruleus with 6–7; Common daisy / Bellis perennis with 8–9; White clover / Trifolium repens with 10–11; 7-spot ladybird / Coccinella septempunctata with 12–13; and Garden snail / Cornu aspersum with 14–15. Both 36 and 37 are printed. Ordering and visual grouping may vary, but missing, duplicated or misassociated entries fail, including omission of species without delivered overviews in tier 6.

The two-page specification functions as the upstream design specification and explicitly states the exact title and subtitle, ages 8–12, #24352A, #DCE5C9, #AD5B3C, 148 × 210 mm pages, two columns per page, 4 mm column gaps, and 6 mm outer margins and safe bands on both sides of the fold. It names actual typefaces rather than generic categories, defines the overview name/three-fact/two-label/question pattern, records the six species' supplied diagnostic features, and gives Pause → Notice → Record plus I noticed, I wonder and Not seen. Choices left open by the commission may vary; omissions or contradictions of fixed specifications fail.

Compare each artwork with the written specification for applicable typography, colour roles, illustration treatment, reader age, content pattern and page geometry. Spread geometry applies to interior spreads; the cover applies the identity and illustration rules. Reflow and subject-specific compositions may vary within the specified system. Material contradictions between the specification and applications fail.

The presentation explicitly repeats the specification's 148 × 210 mm page size, two columns per page, 4 mm gap, 6 mm outer margins and fold bands, ages 8–12, all three exact colour codes and actual typeface names. These facts may appear in a legible reused specification or explanatory text. Implicit visual resemblance, generic type categories, omitted values or inconsistent numbers fail.

Each spread gives Pause, Notice and Record in the specification's order and explicitly communicates quiet observation with an adult from a path or permitted garden while leaving plants rooted and animals where they are. The method spread explains the steps through an illustrated daytime observation. Both records visibly repeat I noticed, I wonder and Not seen and keep observations separate from questions. Concise paraphrases of the reminder are acceptable; merely showing an adult without the required guidance is insufficient.

Compare the two forms: the seven recording spaces retain their positions, the blank remains uncompleted, and the worked entry is headed Practice example — not a field record above the data. Read every practice value: 17 May 2027, 10:20; Practice garden path (invented); Overcast after rain; White clover / Trifolium repens; One leaf had three visible leaflets with pale markings; Sketch one leaf with three leaflets; No movement noticed while looking at the leaf; I could see three leaflets on this one leaf; Are there flower heads hidden by the grass?; Other leaves were partly covered; I did not count them. I noticed and I wonder contain their respective separate responses. Line wrapping may change; substituted values, omitted uncertainty or presenting invented data as a field record fail.

Review the complete video and its duration. It runs for 10 seconds and visibly reuses the actual delivered cover, method spread and robin overview, followed by a discernible blank-to-worked record progression. Pans, crops, transitions and scaling may vary; replacement artwork, missing groups or reversed form progression fail.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation contains at least eight pages and visibly incorporates material from every listed source, including the specification and each individual overview. Blank and worked records appear together on the same page or a facing comparison spread. Multiple artworks may share a presentation page, but missing sources, prose-only claims of reuse or forms separated so their relationship cannot be compared fail.

The cover and all six overviews implement the specification's typography, layout palette and observational illustration treatment. The overviews form one page family with consistent name hierarchy, facts, linked labels, questions and folios.

Method, navigation and recording pages apply the specified grid, typography, palette and applicable fixed labels. The completed record preserves the blank form's field positions and distinction between observations, questions and uncertainty. Method and recording guidance agrees on quiet observation with an adult from a path or permitted garden and leaving living subjects in place.
